newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: U.S. official visits Guatemalan ex-guerrillas.
newsitem.headline: U.S. official visits Guatemalan ex-guerrillas.

text.p: A top U.S. official on Thursday visited two guerrilla disarmament camps where the former enemies of Guatemala's U.S.-backed military regimes welcomed American support for the peace process here.

Amid swirling dust, Thomas "Mack" McLarty, President Bill Clinton's Special Envoy for the Americas, toured the temporary barracks and clinics at Elvira and Claudia camps where 600 former rebels will live for two months and turn in weapons under United Nations scrutiny.

"What we would hope for from the U.S. government is a relationship of respect, collaboration and interest in participating in the development of our region," Commander Santiago, leader of the 331-member Unitary Front, told Reuters.

The camps where about 3,000 guerrillas will disarm were established under a comprehensive series of peace accords signed on Dec. 29, 1996, by the government and leftist rebels of the Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit (URNG), ending 36 years of civil war.
McLarty was in Guatemala for a two-day visit. On Wednesday he addressed business leaders at a Central American-U.S. trade forum.

"I prefer to focus on the present and the future and that's my sense from the Guatemalan people of what they are focusing on," McLarty said when reporters asked whether the United States should apologise for past military interventions in this country.
Through most of nearly four decades of war, the United States covertly and overtly aided the Guatemalan army counterinsurgency campaigns that tried to wipe the guerrillas off the map.
